claims.claim: The paper identity is MLLM-4D: Towards Visual-based Spatial-Temporal Intelligence, arXiv:2603.00515v1, by Yin, Li, Chang, Pun, and Cun.
The paper frames visual 4D spatial-temporal intelligence as understanding the evolution of 3D space over time from visual input.
The framework creates MLLM4D-2M and MLLM4D-R1-30k and uses them for SFT and RFT respectively.
MLLM4D-Bench covers Independent Object Motion, Camera Ego-Motion, and Object-Camera Dynamics, expanded into six QA categories.
Stereo4D metadata includes per-frame camera poses, metric 3D object points, and frame-level descriptions.
Camera center is computed as Center_i=-R_i^T t_i and camera absolute distance is the L2 distance between centers.
Camera relative direction uses d_cam_rel_dir=R_i^T(t_j-t_i) with +X right, +Y down, +Z forward.
Object absolute distance uses the L2 distance between mean object-point centroids.
Object-camera absolute distance is the minimum point-to-camera-center distance across object points.
Object-camera relative distance thresholds the change in nearest object-camera distance into farther, closer, or not moving.
Object-camera relative direction is determined after transforming object points to camera coordinates and comparing lateral/depth changes.
Entity extraction uses Gemini-2.5-Flash, GroundedSAM2, and PixelRefer; the pipeline then applies a physics-based spatial-temporal solver.
SFT uses LoRA and cross-entropy over the reasoning-answer trajectory.
ST-CoT has five stages: objective/temporal anchoring, start-frame state parsing, temporal progression, end-frame verification, and evidence-based synthesis.
The final ST-CoT answer is conditioned on object information, start/end spatial states, motion trajectory, and video evidence.
Accuracy reward is binary, format reward checks structural and coordinate formats, and ST-reward combines camera and object coordinate alignment.
Coordinate alignment reward uses an exponential of mean Euclidean error, and total reward combines accuracy, format, and ST components.
GRPO uses group outputs, normalized group advantages, clipping, and KL regularization against a frozen reference model.
The main backbones are Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct; LoRA rank is 128 and alpha is 256.
The appendix reports one-epoch SFT, about 30K SFT steps, peak learning rate 2e-5, warmup 0.01, global batch size 8, 12 rollouts per RFT question, and about 15K RFT steps.
Training used 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs; SFT/cold start took about 12 hours and RFT about 50 hours.
On MLLM4D-Bench, MLLM-4D Qwen3-VL-8B reports 73.4, 71.9, 76.3, 74.3, 69.2, 70.9 across the six columns and 72.7 average.
On VLM4D, the Qwen3-VL-8B model reports 61.0 overall and the table lists VG-LLM at 57.1 overall.
Table 3 reports 35.3/52.1 for baseline, 59.9/56.2 for SFT without Sec.3 data, 70.1/59.7 for SFT with data, 70.5/61.4 for GRPO without ST-reward, and 72.7/63.1 for GRPO with ST-reward.
Figure 5 reports SFT scaling from 52.1 at 10K to 59.7 at 2M, with 57.7 at 200K; RFT scaling reaches 63.1 at 30K.
Figures 12-17 show qualitative cases where MLLM-4D writes start/end states and temporal evidence while baselines make spatial or temporal mistakes.
The authors identify long video/context limits and monocular depth ambiguity as future-work or limitation concerns.

On the final qualitative pages, MLLM-4D matches the displayed answers in Figure 15 (D, swan not spinning), Figure 16 (A, boy direction), and Figure 17 (C, person holding girl staying in place), while VG-LLM and/or Qwen3-VL select incorrect alternatives.

Figure 16 contains a visible intermediate-explanation mismatch: MLLM-4D's prose says the evidence supports 'towards the camera', while the selected final option is A and the displayed option A is 'left'.

interpretation_anchors.interpretation: The largest reported gain is associated with the data-plus-SFT recipe, while ST-reward adds a smaller but consistent final increment.

interpretation_anchors.interpretation: The contribution is best described as state-trajectory supervision for a video MLLM, not a complete 4D perception or embodied-control solution.
The comparison is a full-system comparison and is not a matched-budget causal test of ST-reward alone.

limitations_of_grounding: The source PDF was visually inspected page-by-page; restricted local tooling prevented extraction of original raster crops, so linked SVG assets are explanatory redraws rather than source-image copies.
The note does not use external web evidence; code availability and released-data status are not independently verified.
The paper's qualitative examples are treated as examples, not as population-level error statistics.
